description: errorBoundary `fallback={<div ...>text/}` — the so-called terse `/}` markup-value closer is the RETIRED trailing-slash closer (§4.4, Appendix E), not a closer: it is refused with E-SYNTAX-050, whose message carries the Appendix E hint "Did you mean `</>`?". The `</>` twin (error-boundary/no-renders-falls-to-fallback) covers the rendering this case used to assert (a no-renders variant falls to the boundary's fallback markup).
rationale: Appendix E (2026-04-09): "Any source file using bare `/` or trailing content`/` closers SHALL be rejected by the compiler with a diagnostic pointing to §4.4. The diagnostic SHALL include a hint: 'Did you mean `</>`?'". ruling:user-voice-scrml.md "⭐ RULED — the `/}` 'terse closer' is the retired trailing-slash closer; Appendix E governs (S482)" — owner: "yes to the /} cleanup, this is bothersome to me because the / only closer was overruled for </> so long ago". This case was a POSITIVE (S237, Peter #22) built on §19.6.2 examples that the 2026-04-09 migration missed; S482 migrated those examples to `</>` and turned the case negative. The positive rendering lives on in the `</>` twin error-boundary/no-renders-falls-to-fallback.
